_about: What children learn in Years 5 to 9 (National Curriculum for England). Years 5 and 6 follow the statutory year-by-year programme; KS3 (Years 7 to 9) is one programme and schools choose the order. Links point to practice on this site.

stages.name: Year 5
maths: Numbers up to 1,000,000; negative numbers in context; rounding; Roman numerals to 1,000
Adding and subtracting numbers with more than 4 digits, and in your head
Multiples, factors, prime numbers, square and cube numbers
Multiplying up to 4 digits by 1 or 2 digits; short division; × and ÷ by 10, 100 and 1,000
Fractions: equivalent fractions, mixed numbers, adding and subtracting, multiplying by whole numbers
Decimals up to 3 decimal places; percentages
Converting metric units; perimeter and area of rectangles; money and time problems
Angles in degrees (acute, obtuse, reflex); angles on a line and round a point; reflection and translation
science: Properties and changes of materials (dissolving, separating, reversible changes)
Earth and space: the Sun, Earth and Moon, day and night
Forces: gravity, air resistance, water resistance, friction, levers, pulleys and gears
Living things and their habitats: life cycles and reproduction
Animals including humans: how humans change as they grow

stages.name: Year 6
maths: Numbers up to 10,000,000; negative numbers; rounding
Long multiplication and long division; order of operations
Fractions: simplifying, adding and subtracting with different denominators, multiplying, dividing by a whole number
Fractions, decimals and percentages, and how they are linked
Algebra: simple formulae, sequences, missing numbers
Converting units; area of triangles and parallelograms; volume of cuboids
Angles in triangles and polygons; circles; nets; coordinates in four quadrants
Pie charts, line graphs and the mean
science: Living things: classifying plants and animals
Animals including humans: the heart, blood and circulation; healthy living
Light: how we see, shadows, reflection
Electricity: circuits, symbols, brighter bulbs and louder buzzers

stages.name: Years 7 to 9
maths: Number: negative numbers, factors and primes, powers and roots, rounding and estimating
Fractions, decimals, percentages, and percentage change
Algebra: expressions, substitution, equations, sequences, straight-line graphs
Ratio, proportion and rates of change, including speed
Geometry: angles and parallel lines, area and volume, circles, transformations, Pythagoras' theorem
Probability and statistics: averages, charts and simple probability
science: Physics: forces, motion and pressure; energy and energy bills; waves (sound and light); electricity and magnetism; particles and density; space
Chemistry: particles, atoms, elements and compounds, mixtures, chemical reactions, acids and alkalis, the periodic table, the Earth and atmosphere
Biology: cells, body systems, nutrition and digestion, respiration and photosynthesis, ecosystems, genetics and evolution

pyp: The IB Primary Years Programme (PYP) doesn't set content year by year in the same way: schools plan their own units of inquiry. The Maths strands (number, pattern and function, measurement, shape and space, data handling) cover very similar skills, so the Years 5 and 6 lists above are a good guide for the last two years of the PYP.
